**Finding: deviation (ASSIGN, high severity)** — submitted.

**What I found**
- **§20(d) (p0142)**: "Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party." — absolute mutual consent gate, no reasonableness standard, no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us.
- **§3(c) (p0033)**: reinforces the bar, prohibiting Sparkling from assigning except as authorized by Garman in writing.
- **No change-of-control provision anywhere** in the document, so Garman has no CoC termination or re-pricing right today. I added confirming language rather than treating this as a separate gap.

**Why it fails the fallback**: the playbook fallback requires at minimum a mutual right to assign to successors on written notice with consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld. A blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out is expressly walk-away territory — it would give Garman a veto over our own corporate transactions.

**Redline (validated ok:true, preferred position, modeled on seed-assign precedent)**
- §20(d): consent "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed"; Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets on written notice; Garman may not assign to a Sparkling competitor; our change of control is not an assignment and triggers no Garman termination, suspension or re-pricing right.
- §3(c): conforming cross-reference "or as permitted by Section 20(d)" so the use restriction does not undercut the new carve-out.
